statement.text:
A formation F is called radical in a class H if F ⊆ H and in every H-group
the product of any two normal F-subgroups belongs to F. Let M be the class of all
saturated hereditary formations of finite groups such that the formation of all finite
supersoluble groups is radical in every element of M. Is it true that M has the largest
(by inclusion) element?                                A. F. Vasil’ev, L. A. Shemetkov
